# H2: Stating causal model

Now we can need to account also for our second hypothesis, namely

*H2: A higher degree of misunderstanding will require a performer to engage in more effortful correction.*

We operationalize degree of misunderstanding as a cosine similarity of performer's target and guesser's answer (PrevAn). The difficulty with our data structure is that PrevAn is a variable that has values only for second and third correction (i.e., there is no previous answer for the first performance). If we left it unchange, the model will eventually get rid of all NA values, which means we will loose the relationship between effort in second and first communicative attempt. To avoid this, we will create a new variable which we call *Effort Change*. We will simply calculate the change from effort in communicative attempt x to communicative attempt x+1. We will still loose communicative attempt 1, but the change that will be associated with CommAtt==2 already encapsulates the relationship towards this attempt.

We also need a new DAG. Essentially, what we said will influence CommAtt in H1, will now also influence PrevAn because they are tightly related. For instance, more extroverted people can be expected to be better guessers, therefore the similarity of the previous answer will be higher.

```{r dag h2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

daggy_h2 <- dagitty('dag {
EffChange [outcome,pos="0,0"]
PrevAn [exposure,pos="-2,0"]
Big5 [pos="-1.5,1"]
CommAtt [pos="0,-1.5"]
Conc [pos="-2,-1.5"]
Expr [pos="-1.5,-1.5"]
Fam [pos="-0.5,1"]
Pcn [pos="-1,2"]
TrNum [pos="-2.5,-1.5"]
Mod [pos="-1,0.5"]

Big5 -> PrevAn     
Big5 -> EffChange
CommAtt -> EffChange
Conc -> Expr
Expr -> PrevAn
Expr -> EffChange
Fam -> PrevAn
Fam -> EffChange
Mod -> EffChange
Mod -> PrevAn
Pcn -> Big5
Pcn -> PrevAn 
Pcn -> EffChange
Pcn -> Fam
TrNum -> PrevAn
TrNum -> EffChange
Conc -> PrevAn
Conc -> EffChange
PrevAn -> EffChange
PrevAn -> CommAtt
}')

```

```{r dag h2 adjustset, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
# Use ggdag for a cleaner visualization
d2 <- ggdag(daggy_h2, text = TRUE, use_labels = "name") +
  theme_dag() +
  ggtitle("Causal DAG for Effort Change") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

d2
```

```{r dag h2 adjustset, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE}

dagitty::adjustmentSets(daggy_h2, exposure = "PrevAn", outcome = "EffChange")

```

The adjustment set is identical to the one of H1. Note that we are here omitting arrows going from all these variables to ComAtt. Since PrevAn affects CommAtt, and not the other way, we do not need to block this path to avoid confounds. However, if we want to asses direct effect of PrevAn on EffChange, we have to add CommAtt to the model as well.

# H2: Modeling

## Var 1: Cumulative torque

```{r h2 loading data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# load our data back if we lost them
final_data <- data_feat

```

### Data wrangling I

```{r effort change ratio, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Calculate Effort Change (Difference)
final_data_2 <- final_data %>%
  group_by(pcn_ID, concept) %>%
  mutate(
    Effort_1 = arm_moment_sum_change_integral[correction_info == 'c0'][1],  # Effort for attempt 1
    Effort_2 = arm_moment_sum_change_integral[correction_info == 'c1'][1],  # Effort for attempt 2
    Effort_3 = arm_moment_sum_change_integral[correction_info == 'c2'][1],  # Effort for attempt 3
    Effort_Change_1_to_2 = case_when(
      correction_info == 'c1' & !is.na(Effort_1) ~ arm_moment_sum_change_integral - Effort_1,  
      # Change from 1st to 2nd attempt
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    Effort_Change_2_to_3 = case_when(
      correction_info == 'c2' & !is.na(Effort_2) ~ arm_moment_sum_change_integral - Effort_2,  
      # Change from 2nd to 3rd attempt
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Collide changes into a single column
final_data_2 <- final_data_2 %>%
  mutate(
    Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral = coalesce(Effort_Change_1_to_2, Effort_Change_2_to_3)
  ) 

# Remove unnecessary columns
final_data_2 <- subset(final_data_2, select = -c(Effort_1, Effort_2, Effort_3, Effort_Change_1_to_2, Effort_Change_2_to_3)) 

# View the result
head(final_data_2, n=15)

```

```{r h2 factorizing, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
final_data$modality <- as.factor(final_data$modality)
final_data$pcn_ID <- as.factor(final_data$pcn_ID)
final_data$concept <- as.factor(final_data$concept)
```

### Model 3 - Varying slopes and intercepts

We are now going to procede with the same steps as in models for H1. 

Do we have enough data points?


Let's add random slopes. 

```{r}

if (file.exists(here(models, "h2.m3_torq_cum.rds"))){
  
  h2.m3_torq_cum <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m3_torq_cum.rds"))
  h2.m3_torq_cum_R2 <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m3_torq_cum_R2.rds"))
  
} else {
  
  h2.m3_torq_cum <- brm(Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral ~ 1 + answer_prev_dist_z + correction_info + Familiarity + BFI_extra + expressibility_z + Modality_dummy + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | pcn_ID)  + (1 | SessionID) + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | concept) + (1 | TrialNumber_c), 
                data = df_ges,
                family = student(),
                iter = 2000,
                cores = 4)
  
  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.m3_torq_cum <- add_criterion(h2.m3_torq_cum, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.m3_torq_cum_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.m3_torq_cum)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.m3_torq_cum, here(models, "h2.m3_torq_cum.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.m3_torq_cum_R2, here(models, "h2.m3_torq_cum_R2.rds"))
  
}

# Summary
summary(h2.m3_torq_cum)



```

### Model 4 - Adding interactions

Last thing we do with linear models is that we add interactions. As mentioned in the preregistrated script, we can consider:

-   PrevAn x Modality - similarity affects the change in effort differently (e.g., vocal might still require more effort)

-   PrevAn x Expressibility - similarity in relation to effort might matter only for highly expressible concepts, and low expressible concepts are difficult to express, so also difficult to exaggerate

### Splines 1 - fitting b-splines

In the previous model for H1, we were able to spot possible non-linear trends by contrast coding of the communicative attempts whereby each level was defined relative to the two remaining. Now, we are dealing with situation where both outcome variable and the main predictor are continuous variable. Also here we might expect nonlinear patterns in their relationship. For instance, it might be the case that for answers that are completely off, people do not feel motivated to put in more effort, and some kind of sensible 'threshold' needs to be reached for the effort to increase to resolve misunderstanding, and then again decrease when the answer is very similar.

We will use a combination of B-splines and Bayesian GAMs to prepare some models and try them fit to the synthetic data. 

```{r h2 plot nonlinear, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

ggplot(df_ges, aes(x = answer_prev_dist, y = Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "blue") +  # Scatter points
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", se = FALSE) +  # loess for potential nonlinearity
  labs(x = "Previous Answer Similarity (PrevAn)", 
       y = "Effort (Eff)", 
       title = "Relationship between Effort and Previous Answer Similarity") +
  theme_minimal()

```

B-splines allow to build up wiggly functions from more simple components which are called 'basis functions' (B). They divide a full range of predictor into parts and assign a parameter to each part. The parameters are gradually turned on and off in a way that makes their sum into a curve. Unlike polynomial regression, b-splines do not transform predictor, but they invent a series of new synthetic predictor variables. Each of them then exists only to gradually turn a specific parameter on and off within a specific range of the real predictor variable. Each of these synthetic variables is called a basis function B. See more in Richard McElreath's Statistical Rethinking [@mcelreath18].

We are using the [code](https://bookdown.org/content/4857/geocentric-models.html) from Solomon Kurz's adaptation of this book.

```{r h2 datawrangle, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Get rid of NAs in the predictor
d <-
  df_ges %>% 
  drop_na(answer_prev_dist)

# And convert all that is necessary to factor/numerical
#d$CommAtt <- as.factor(d$CommAtt)
#d$Modality <- as.factor(d$Modality)
#d$Participant <- as.factor(d$Participant)
#d$Concept <- as.factor(d$Concept)
#d$TrialNumber <- as.numeric(d$TrialNumber) 

```

Here we can see summary of each predictor

```{r h2 datawrangle 2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

d %>% 
  select_if(is.numeric) %>%  # Select only numeric columns
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "key", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(key) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd   = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    ll   = quantile(value, probs = 0.055, na.rm = TRUE),
    ul   = quantile(value, probs = 0.945, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), round, digits = 2))

head(d, n=10)

```

Now we need to specify knots that function as pivots for number of different basis functions. The B variable then tells you which knot you are close to.

```{r h2 knots, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

num_knots <- 7
knot_list <- quantile(d$answer_prev_dist_z, probs = seq(from = 0, to = 1, length.out = num_knots))
knot_list

```

Now we can see how we chopped the data by the knots

```{r h2 knot plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

d %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = answer_prev_dist_z, y = Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = knot_list, color = "white", alpha = 1/2) +
  geom_point(color = "#ffb7c5", alpha = 1/2) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#4f455c"),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

```

Now we need to specify the polynomial degree which determines how parameters interact to produce the spline.

For degree 1, two basis functions combine at each point. For degree 2, three functions combine at each point. For degree 3, four combine.

```{r b-spline, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

B <- bs(d$answer_prev_dist_z,
        knots = knot_list[-c(1, num_knots)], 
        degree = 3, # cubic spline
        intercept = TRUE)

```

This is how cubic spline with 7 knots look like

```{r b-spline plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# wrangle a bit
b <-
  B %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  set_names(str_c(0, 1:4), 5:9) %>%  
  bind_cols(select(d, answer_prev_dist_z)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-answer_prev_dist_z,
               names_to = "bias_function",
               values_to = "bias")

# plot
b %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = answer_prev_dist_z, y = bias, group = bias_function)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = knot_list, color = "white", alpha = 1/2) +
  geom_line(color = "#ffb7c5", alpha = 1/2, linewidth = 1.5) +
  ylab("bias value") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#4f455c"),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

```

We will now add this B matrix into the data to be able to further use it in the models

```{r b-spline 2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

d2 <-
  d %>% 
  mutate(B = B) 

# take a look at the structure of `d3
d2 %>% glimpse()

```

The B matrix is now a matrix column which contains the same number of rows as the others, but has also 9 columns within that columns. Each of them correspond to one synthetic B variable.

We can now use this matrix to fit our model

```{r h2.s1 run, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

if (file.exists(here(models, "h2.s1_torq_cum.rds"))){
  
  h2.s1_torq_cum <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.s1_torq_cum.rds"))
  h2.s1_torq_cum_R2 <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.s1_torq_cum_R2.rds"))
  
} else {

  h2.s1_torq_cum <- 
    brm(data = d2,
        family = gaussian,
        Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral ~ 1 + B,
        prior = c(prior(normal(100, 10), class = Intercept),
                  prior(normal(0, 10), class = b),
                  prior(exponential(1), class = sigma)),
        iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, chains = 4, cores = 4,
        seed = 4)

  
  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.s1_torq_cum <- add_criterion(h2.s1_torq_cum, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.s1_torq_cum_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.s1_torq_cum)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.s1_torq_cum, here(models, "h2.s1_torq_cum.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.s1_torq_cum_R2, here(models, "h2.s1_torq_cum_R2.rds"))
  
}

print(h2.s1_torq_cum)

```

It's a bit difficult to see what is going on so let's just plot it

```{r h2.s1 plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

post <- as_draws_df(h2.s1_torq_cum)

post %>% 
  select(b_B1:b_B9) %>% 
  set_names(c(str_c(0, 1:4), 5:9)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "bias_function") %>% 
  group_by(bias_function) %>% 
  summarise(weight = mean(value)) %>% 
  full_join(b, by = "bias_function") %>% 
  
  # plot
  ggplot(aes(x = answer_prev_dist_z, y = bias * weight, group = bias_function)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = knot_list, color = "white", alpha = 1/2) +
  geom_line(color = "#ffb7c5", alpha = 1/2, linewidth = 1.5) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#4f455c"),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) 

```

Now with the predictor

```{r h2.s1 plot2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

f <- fitted(h2.s1_torq_cum)

f %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  bind_cols(d2) %>% 
  
  ggplot(aes(x = answer_prev_dist_z, y = Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral, ymin = Q2.5, ymax = Q97.5)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = knot_list, color = "white", alpha = 1/2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = fixef(h2.s1_torq_cum)[1, 1], color = "white", linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(color = "#ffb7c5", alpha = 1/2) +
  geom_ribbon(fill = "white", alpha = 2/3) +
  labs(x = "Previous Answer",
       y = "Effort Change") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#4f455c"),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

```

Now let's check some diagnostics

```{r h2.s1 check, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

plot(h2.s1_torq_cum)
# looks good

pp_check(h2.s1_torq_cum, type = "dens_overlay")
# because we used only main predictor, we can see quite a bad result of the posterior predictive distribution, but we will work on that

pp_check(h2.s1_torq_cum, type = "error_scatter_avg")
# high residual error for both low and high values

h2.s1_torq_cum_R2
# explained variance essentialy 0

```

### Splines 2 - Bayesian GAMs

Now we will use a different workflow, using smooth functions with `brms` package. Brms allow for non-linear models by borrowing functions from `mgcv` package [@wood17]

This is how priors should look like for one of these functions

```{r h2.s2 priors, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

get_prior(data = d2,
          family = gaussian,
          Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral ~ 1 + s(answer_prev_dist_z))
```

At this point, I will just keep priors at default

```{r h2.s2 run, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

if (file.exists(here(models, "h2.s2_torq_cum.rds"))){
  
  h2.s2_torq_cum <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.s2_torq_cum.rds"))
  h2.s2_torq_cum_R2 <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.s2_torq_cum_R2.rds"))
  
} else {
  
  h2.s2_torq_cum <-
    brm(data = d2,
        family = student(),
        Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral ~ 1 + s(answer_prev_dist_z, bs = "bs", k = 19),
        iter = 2000, 
        warmup = 1000, 
        chains = 4, 
        cores = 4,
        seed = 4,
        control = list(adapt_delta = .99)
        )

  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.s2_torq_cum <- add_criterion(h2.s2_torq_cum, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.s2_torq_cum_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.s2_torq_cum)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.s2_torq_cum, here(models, "h2.s2_torq_cum.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.s2_torq_cum_R2, here(models, "h2.s2_torq_cum_R2.rds"))

  }

# Summary
summary(h2.s2_torq_cum)

```

Now we can proceed as we usually do

```{r h2.s2 check, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

plot(h2.s2_torq_cum)
# looks good

plot(conditional_effects(h2.s2_torq_cum), points = TRUE)
# again, we see similar (non-linear) trend 

pp_check(h2.s2_torq_cum, type = "dens_overlay")
# looks good

pp_check(h2.s2_torq_cum, type = "error_scatter_avg")
# still weird

h2.s2_torq_cum_R2
# explained variance 2%

```

### Splines 3 - GAMs with f+r effects

Now let's use the same model, but adding our other predictors

```{r h2.s3 run, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

if (file.exists(here(models, "h2.s3_torq_cum.rds"))){
  
  h2.s3_torq_cum <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.s3_torq_cum.rds"))
  h2.s3_torq_cum_R2 <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.s3_torq_cum_R2.rds"))
  
} else {
  
  h2.s3_torq_cum <- 
    brm(
      data = d2,
      family = student(),
      Effort_Change_arm_moment_integral ~ 1 +
        s(answer_prev_dist_z, bs = "bs", k = 19) +  # Smooth for Previous Answer similarity
        correction_info + Familiarity + BFI_extra + expressibility_z + Modality_dummy + 
        (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | pcn_ID)  + (1 | SessionID) + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | concept) + (1 | TrialNumber_c),
      iter = 2000, 
      warmup = 1000, 
      chains = 4, 
      cores = 4,
      seed = 4,
      control = list(adapt_delta = .99)
    )

  
  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.s3_torq_cum <- add_criterion(h2.s3_torq_cum, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.s3_torq_cum_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.s3_torq_cum)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.s3_torq_cum, here(models, "h2.s3_torq_cum.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.s3_torq_cum_R2, here(models, "h2.s3_torq_cum_R2.rds"))

}

summary(h2.s3_torq_cum)


```

```{r h2.s3 check, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}


plot(h2.s3_torq_cum)
# looks ok

plot(conditional_effects(h2.s3_torq_cum), points = TRUE)
# now the ffect of PrevAn looks a bit different because we are back to using z-scored version

pp_check(h2.s3_torq_cum, type = "dens_overlay")
# looks good

pp_check(h2.s3_torq_cum, type = "error_scatter_avg")
# still not what we would like

h2.s3_torq_cum_R2
# 1 %


```

### Model 5 - Previous effort as a predictor instead of change

```{r}

df_ges <- df_ges |>
  arrange(pcn_ID, concept, TrialNumber) |>
  group_by(pcn_ID, concept) |>
  mutate(
    effort_previous_moment_integral = lag(arm_moment_sum_change_integral, n = 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Test

df_ges |>
  filter(pcn_ID == df_ges$pcn_ID[1], concept == df_ges$concept[1]) |>
  select(pcn_ID, concept, TrialNumber, correction, 
         arm_moment_sum_change_integral, effort_previous_moment_integral)


# Re-cc
df_ges <- df_ges |> filter(correction != 'c0')
df_ges$correction <- factor(df_ges$correction, 
                                   levels = c('c1', 'c2'))

contrasts(df_ges$correction) <- MASS::contr.sdif(2) 

# z-score again 

df_ges <-
  df_ges |>
  mutate(answer_prev_dist_z = (answer_prev_dist - mean(answer_prev_dist))/ sd(df_ges$answer_prev_dist, na.rm = T)) |>
  ungroup()

# center previous effort
df_ges <- df_ges |>
  mutate(
    effort_previous_moment_integral_c = effort_previous_moment_integral - mean(effort_previous_moment_integral, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```


We will use the priors from H1, and add priors for cosine_similarity and previous_effort


```{r}


priors_h2m5_torq_cum <- c(
  set_prior("normal(5, 2)", class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "answer_prev_dist_z"), # new
  set_prior("normal(0,0.25)", class = "b", coef = "BFI_extra"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "correction2M1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.35)", class = "b", coef = "expressibility_z"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.25)", class = "b", coef = "Familiarity"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "Modality_dummy1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.15)", class = "sd"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "sigma"),
  # Random effect SDs: differentiated by grouping factor
  # Participants: largest expected source of variation
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "pcn_ID"),
  # Concepts: moderate
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "concept"),
  # Trial number: small drift
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.1)", class = "sd", group = "TrialNumber_c")
)
  
```

Now we can fit the model with effort as IV, and previous_effort as predictor in interaction with the answer. 

```{r}


if (file.exists(here(models, "h2.m5_torqi_cum.rds"))){
  
  h2.m5_torq_cum <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m5_torq_cum.rds"))
  h2.m5_torq_cum_R2 <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m5_torq_cum_R2.rds"))
  
} else {
  
  h2.m5_torq_cum <- brm(arm_moment_sum_change_integral ~ 1 + answer_prev_dist_z + correction + Familiarity + BFI_extra + expressibility_z + Modality_dummy + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | pcn_ID)  + (1 | SessionID) + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | concept) + (1 | TrialNumber_c),
                data = df_ges,
                family = lognormal(),
                prior = priors_h2m5_torq_cum,
                iter = 4000,
                cores = 4)

  
  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.m5_torq_cum <- add_criterion(h2.m5_torq_cum, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.m5_torq_cum_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.m5_torq_cum)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.m5_torq_cum, here(models, "h2.m5_torq_cum.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.m5_torq_cum_R2, here(models, "h2.m5_torq_cum_R2.rds"))

  
}

# Summary
summary(h2.m5_torq_cum)


```

### Diagnostics I

Before we proceed further, let's do first round of diagnostics

```{r h2 diagnostics, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

model_list <- list(h2.m0_torq_cum, h2.m1_torq_cum, h2.m2_torq_cum, h2.m3_torq_cum, h2.m3p_torq_cum, h2.m4_torq_cum, h2.s1_torq_cum, h2.s2_torq_cum, h2.s3_torq_cum, h2.m5_torq_cum)

```

#### Rhat

```{r h2 rhat, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Extract R-hat values for each model
rhat_list <- lapply(model_list, function(model) {
  rhat_values <- rhat(model)
  data.frame(model = deparse(substitute(model)), 
             max_rhat = max(rhat_values), 
             min_rhat = min(rhat_values))
})

# Combine and inspect
do.call(rbind, rhat_list)

```

All Rhat values look good except the last one

### ESS

Effective sample size tells how many independent samples the model has effectively drawn from the PD. Low ESS suggests autocorrelation (i.e., sample explores one part of posterior), while high ESS means good mix

```{r h2 ess, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Extract n_eff values for each model
neff_ratio_list <- lapply(model_list, function(model) {
  neff_values <- neff_ratio(model)              # Here we calculate ratio (not the raw number of effective samples)
  data.frame(model = deparse(substitute(model)), 
             min_neff = min(neff_values), 
             max_neff = max(neff_values),
             mean_neff = mean(neff_values))
               
})

# Combine and inspect
do.call(rbind, neff_ratio_list)

```

They all look good expect the last one again

### LOO & WAIC

```{r h2 loo, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

l <- loo_compare(h2.m0_torq_cum, h2.m1_torq_cum, h2.m2_torq_cum, h2.m3_torq_cum, h2.m3p_torq_cum, h2.m4_torq_cum, h2.s1_torq_cum, h2.s2_torq_cum, h2.s3_torq_cum, h2.m5_torq_cum, criterion = "loo")

print(l, simplify = F)

```
Assessed by LOO, here we see that the last one (with previous_effort as FF) is actually the best.

```{r h2 waic, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

w <- loo_compare(h2.m0_torq_cum, h2.m1_torq_cum, h2.m2_torq_cum, h2.m3_torq_cum, h2.m3p_torq_cum, h2.m4_torq_cum, h2.s1_torq_cum, h2.s2_torq_cum, h2.s3_torq_cum, h2.m5_torq_cum, criterion = "waic")

print(w, simplify = F)

# see Solomon Kurz
cbind(waic_diff = w[,1] * -2,
      se = w[,2] * 2)

```

Plot the comparison

```{r h2 waic plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

w[, 7:8] %>% 
  data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("model_name") %>% 
  mutate(model_name = fct_reorder(model_name, waic, .desc = T)) %>% 
  
  ggplot(aes(x = waic, y = model_name, 
             xmin = waic - se_waic, 
             xmax = waic + se_waic)) +
  geom_pointrange(color = carto_pal(7, "BurgYl")[7], 
                  fill = carto_pal(7, "BurgYl")[5], shape = 21) +
  labs(title = "WAIC plot",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

```

Here we see identical results

```{r h2 weights, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

model_weights(h2.m0_torq_cum, h2.m1_torq_cum, h2.m2_torq_cum, h2.m3_torq_cum, h2.m3p_torq_cum, h2.m4_torq_cum, h2.s1_torq_cum, h2.s2_torq_cum, h2.s3_torq_cum, h2.m5_torq_cum, weights = "waic") %>%
```

### Data wrangling

```{r}

df_ges <- df_ges |>
  arrange(pcn_ID, concept, TrialNumber) |>
  group_by(pcn_ID, concept) |>
  mutate(
    effort_previous_moment_peak_mean = lag(arm_moment_sum_change_peak_mean, n = 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Re-cc
df_ges <- df_ges |> filter(correction_info != 'c0')
df_ges <- df_ges |> filter(correction_info != 'c0_only')
df_ges$correction_info <- factor(df_ges$correction_info, 
                                   levels = c('c1', 'c2'))

contrasts(df_ges$correction_info) <- MASS::contr.sdif(2) 

# z-score again 
df_ges <-
  df_ges |>
  mutate(answer_prev_dist_z = (answer_prev_dist - mean(answer_prev_dist))/ sd(df_ges$answer_prev_dist, na.rm = T)) |>
  ungroup()

# center previous effort
df_ges <- df_ges |>
  mutate(
    effort_previous_moment_peak_mean_c = effort_previous_moment_peak_mean - mean(effort_previous_moment_peak_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```

### Model 5 - Previous effort

We will use the priors from H1, and add priors for cosine_similarity and previous_effort

```{r}


priors_h2m5_torq_in <- c(
  set_prior("normal(-1, 0.5)", class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "answer_prev_dist_z"), # new
  set_prior("normal(0,0.25)", class = "b", coef = "BFI_extra"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "correction2M1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.35)", class = "b", coef = "expressibility_z"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.25)", class = "b", coef = "Familiarity"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "Modality_dummy1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.15)", class = "sd"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "sigma"),
  # Random effect SDs: differentiated by grouping factor
  # Participants: largest expected source of variation
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "pcn_ID"),
  # Concepts: moderate
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "concept"),
  # Trial number: small drift
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.1)", class = "sd", group = "TrialNumber_c")
)

  
```

Now we can fit the model with effort as IV, and previous_effort as predictor in interaction with the answer. 

```{r}

} else {
  
  h2.m5_torq_in <- brm(arm_moment_sum_change_peak_mean ~ 1 + answer_prev_dist_z + correction + Familiarity + BFI_extra + expressibility_z + Modality_dummy + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | pcn_ID)  + (1 | SessionID) + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | concept) + (1 | TrialNumber_c),
                data = df_ges,
                family = lognormal(),
                prior = priors_h2m5_torq_in,
                iter = 2000,
                cores = 4)

  
  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.m5_torq_in <- add_criterion(h2.m5_torq_in, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.m5_torq_in_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.m5_torq_in)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.m5_torq_in, here(models, "h2.m5_torq_in.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.m5_torq_in_R2, here(models, "h2.m5_torq_in_R2.rds"))

  
}

# Summary
summary(h2.m5_torq_in)


```

## Envelope

Prepare the data

First we again prepare the data

```{r h1 factorizing env, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Get rid of vocal modality (torque is relevant only for gesture-only and multimodal condition)
df_voc <- data_feat |> filter(modality != 'gesture')

# Dummy code modality
df_voc$Modality_dummy <- ifelse(df_voc$modality == "multimodal", 1, 0)
df_voc$Modality_dummy <- as.factor(df_voc$Modality_dummy)

# Create column TrialNumber by extracting third element from TrialID
df_voc$TrialNumber <- sapply(strsplit(df_voc$TrialID, "_"), function(x) x[3])
df_voc$TrialNumber <- as.numeric(df_voc$TrialNumber)  # Ensure TrialNumber is numeric

# Create sessionID by taking first element
df_voc$SessionID <- sapply(strsplit(df_voc$TrialID, "_"), function(x) x[1])
df_voc$SessionID <- as.factor(df_voc$SessionID)

# The rest as factor
df_voc$correction <- as.factor(df_voc$correction)
df_voc$pcn_ID <- as.factor(df_voc$pcn_ID)
df_voc$concept <- as.factor(df_voc$concept)

# Contrast-coding of categorical variables - correction
df_voc <- df_voc |> filter(correction != 'c0_only')
df_voc <- df_voc |> filter(correction != 'c0')

df_voc$correction <- factor(df_voc$correction, 
                                   levels = c('c1', 'c2'))

contrasts(df_voc$correction) <- MASS::contr.sdif(2) 

# Center trial number
df_voc$TrialNumber_c <- df_voc$TrialNumber - median(range(df_voc$TrialNumber))

# Z-score familiarity to be compatible with BFI
df_voc$Familiarity <- scale(df_voc$Familiarity, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE) |> as.numeric()

# Z-score previous answer
df_voc <-
  df_voc |>
  mutate(answer_prev_dist_z = (answer_prev_dist - mean(answer_prev_dist))/ sd(df_voc$answer_prev_dist, na.rm = T)) |>
  ungroup()

# Z-score expressibility within modality
df_voc <-
  df_voc |>
  group_by(modality) |>
  mutate(expressibility_z = (expressibility - mean(expressibility))/ sd(df_voc$expressibility, na.rm = T)) |>
  ungroup()

```

```{r}
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "correction2M1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.35)", class = "b", coef = "expressibility_z"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.25)", class = "b", coef = "Familiarity"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "Modality_dummy1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.15)", class = "sd"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "sigma"),
  # Random effect SDs: differentiated by grouping factor
  # Participants: largest expected source of variation
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "pcn_ID"),
  # Concepts: moderate
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "concept"),
  # Trial number: small drift
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.1)", class = "sd", group = "TrialNumber_c")
)

  
```

Now we can fit the model with effort as IV, and previous_effort as predictor in interaction with the answer. 

```{r}


if (file.exists(here(models, "h2.m5_envi_in.rds"))){
  
  h2.m5_env_in <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m5_env_in.rds"))
  h2.m5_env_in_R2 <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m5_env_in_R2.rds"))
  
} else {
  
  h2.m5_env_in <- brm(envelope_norm_peak_mean ~ 1 + answer_prev_dist_z + correction + Familiarity + BFI_extra + expressibility_z + Modality_dummy + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | pcn_ID)  + (1 | SessionID) + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | concept) + (1 | TrialNumber_c),
                data = df_voc,
                family = lognormal(),
                prior = priors_h2m5_env_in,
                iter = 2000,
                cores = 4)

  
  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.m5_env_in <- add_criterion(h2.m5_env_in, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.m5_env_in_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.m5_env_in)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.m5_env_in, here(models, "h2.m5_env_in.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.m5_env_in_R2, here(models, "h2.m5_env_in_R2.rds"))

  
}

# Summary
summary(h2.m5_env_in)


```

## COPc

Now we prepare dataset for this variable

```{r}


# Get rid of vocal modality (torque is relevant only for gesture-only and multimodal condition)
df_all <- data_feat

# Create column TrialNumber by extracting third element from TrialID
df_all$TrialNumber <- sapply(strsplit(df_all$TrialID, "_"), function(x) x[3])
df_all$TrialNumber <- as.numeric(df_all$TrialNumber)  # Ensure TrialNumber is numeric

# Create sessionID by taking first element
df_all$SessionID <- sapply(strsplit(df_all$TrialID, "_"), function(x) x[1])
df_all$SessionID <- as.factor(df_all$SessionID)

# The rest as factor
df_all$correction <- as.factor(df_all$correction)
df_all$pcn_ID <- as.factor(df_all$pcn_ID)
df_all$concept <- as.factor(df_all$concept)
df_all$modality <- as.factor(df_all$modality)

# Contrast-code multimodality
contrasts(df_all$modality) <- contr.sum(3)/2

#          [,1] [,2]
#gesture     0.5  0.0
#multimodal  0.0  0.5
#vocal      -0.5 -0.5

# Contrast-coding of categorical variables - correction
df_all <- df_all |> filter(correction != 'c0_only')
df_all <- df_all |> filter(correction != 'c0')
df_all$correction <- factor(df_all$correction, 
                                   levels = c('c1', 'c2'))

contrasts(df_all$correction) <- MASS::contr.sdif(2) 

# Center trial number
df_all$TrialNumber_c <- df_all$TrialNumber - median(range(df_all$TrialNumber))

# Z-score familiarity to be compatible with BFI
df_all$Familiarity <- scale(df_all$Familiarity, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE) |> as.numeric()

# Z-score expressibility within modality
df_all <-
  df_all |>
  group_by(modality) |>
  mutate(expressibility_z = (expressibility - mean(expressibility))/ sd(df_all$expressibility, na.rm = T)) |>
  ungroup()

# Z-score previous answer
df_all <-
  df_all |>
  mutate(answer_prev_dist_z = (answer_prev_dist - mean(answer_prev_dist))/ sd(df_all$answer_prev_dist, na.rm = T)) |>
  ungroup()



```

### Cummulative


```{r}

priors_h2m5_cop_cum <- c(
  set_prior("normal(8, 2)", class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "answer_prev_dist_z"), # new
  set_prior("normal(0,0.25)", class = "b", coef = "BFI_extra"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "correction2M1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.35)", class = "b", coef = "expressibility_z"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.25)", class = "b", coef = "Familiarity"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "modality1"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.5)", class = "b", coef = "modality2"),
  set_prior("normal(0,0.15)", class = "sd"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "sigma"),
  # Random effect SDs: differentiated by grouping factor
  # Participants: largest expected source of variation
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "pcn_ID"),
  # Concepts: moderate
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.35)", class = "sd", group = "concept"),
  # Trial number: small drift
  set_prior("normal(0, 0.1)", class = "sd", group = "TrialNumber_c")
)

  
```

Now we can fit the model with effort as IV, and previous_effort as predictor in interaction with the answer. 

```{r}


if (file.exists(here(models, "h2.m5_cop_cum.rds"))){
  
  h2.m5_cop_cum <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m5_env_cum.rds"))
  h2.m5_cop_cum_R2 <- readRDS(here(models, "h2.m5_cop_cum_R2.rds"))
  
} else {
  
  h2.m5_cop_cum <- brm(COPc_integral ~ 1 + answer_prev_dist_z + correction + Familiarity + BFI_extra + expressibility_z + modality + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | pcn_ID)  + (1 | SessionID) + (1 + answer_prev_dist_z | concept) + (1 | TrialNumber_c),
                data = df_all,
                family = lognormal(),
                prior = priors_h2m5_cop_cum,
                iter = 2000,
                cores = 4)

  
  # Add criterions for later diagnostics
  h2.m5_cop_cum <- add_criterion(h2.m5_cop_cum, criterion = c("loo", "waic"))
  
  # Calculate also variance explained (R^2)
  h2.m5_cop_cum_R2 <- bayes_R2(h2.m5_cop_cum)
  
  # Save both as objects
  saveRDS(h2.m5_cop_cum, here(models, "h2.m5_cop_cum.rds"))
  saveRDS(h2.m5_cop_cum_R2, here(models, "h2.m5_cop_cum_R2.rds"))

  
}

# Summary
summary(h2.m5_cop_cum)
```
